followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the nature of the task and the relevant capability scores.

The task — pulling major topics and key themes out of an essay — is essentially an extraction and summarization job. On those two internal evals, Dunlin leads by margins well outside the 2.0-point variance band:

- **Extraction & Retrieval:** 85.3 (Dunlin) vs 78.5 (Avocet) — a ~7-point gap
- **Summarization:** 86.4 (Dunlin) vs 79.9 (Avocet) — a ~6.5-point gap

Dunlin also leads broadly on the public benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, IFEval, Arena-Hard), so it's the stronger general performer here.

The other factor I considered was task preference — Avocet has a strong aversion to harm-adjacent content and a strong appetite for open-ended creative work. But neither applies: a history essay on the civil rights movement is benign, factual material, not distasteful or adversarial, and topic-extraction isn't open-ended invention. So Avocet's distinguishing preferences gave it no advantage for this query.

With preferences neutral and capability clearly favoring Dunlin on exactly the skills this task needs, Dunlin was the straightforward pick.
